utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest last night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Judge Argibay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Karnavas: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I want to pick up where we left off yesterday. And as you will recall, we were speaking about your activities of searching the terrain. Now, let me show you a document what has been -- what is marked as P490. It has been admitted into evidence already. If you could look at that. Do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what is this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A daily combat report of the 15th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, is there any -- could you please direct our attention to any relevant paragraph with respect to your unit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here in part of para 2, it says that on that day our forces were still searching the terrain in accordance with your order, and the line is now from Lupoglav, Susnjari, Prijanska Kosa and so on. In relation to this, I can say that on that day, as far as I remember, we did not emerge at this Lupoglav feature or Susnjari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in looking at this daily combat report, is this accurate or inaccurate with respect to what your troops were involved in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let me show you now what is marked as P496. First we're going to look at it. Let me know when you're ready to discuss it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand the question. When did I review what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you finished reviewing it, let me know so we can discuss this. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a daily combat report addressed to the command of the Drina Corps, dated 16th July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I could direct your attention to paragraph 1. Is that relevant in any way to where your units were located, and if so, could you please discuss it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was relevant only inasmuch as it happened in the area of my right neighbour, right-hand neighbour, the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you involved at all in those activities that are mentioned in paragraph 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, for the record I want you to read slowly the first sentence of the first paragraph so we have a correct translation. The first sentence of the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Part of the units continued to search the terrain in the area they had been given orders for."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me stop you here. In the English translation it reflects that the units are searching the terrain in the above areas that are mentioned in paragraph 1. Is that what this reflects in the original version, in the original language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what it says. This relates primarily to the prior order, which we discussed yesterday, the order for terrain search.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I just wanted to point out this rather significant error in translation of this particular portion, which may be misleading. Anything else that's relevant to your particular unit, your troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One item says that preparations have been made to send two companies belonging to the 1st Zvornik Brigade and the reconnaissance or scouting platoon of the 1st Infantry Battalion. As for this scouting platoon or reconnaissance platoon, I can say that they were not sent to the Zvornik area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So that's incorrect as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I believe it says here that a company was engaged -- if we look into paragraph 2, I believe it's the third sentence. It says: "Since the MUP, Ministry of Interior unit, was pulled out this morning from the Kravica/Konjevic Polje direction, a company was engaged at 1400 hours to block this direction." My question, sir, is: Were you ordered or did you send a company to carry out those activities, as reflected in this daily combat report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I don't have anything more on this document. Now, I want to go through some more reports before we go back to the map that we were discussing yesterday. And if I could show you what has been marked as P484. I'll be discussing that with a couple of other documents. If you could look at that very briefly, do you know what this document is, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a request for the relief of units that are part of the 4th Drina Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, why is that significant at all to the Bratunac Brigade and perhaps even more specifically to your battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is significant in as much a part of our forces were engaged in that area, the area of Trnovo, and it will become important later at a point when I received orders to send some of my troops there. However, since orders replaced each other very quickly, during that day, on the 16th, I received a number of orders that superceded each other; in other words, they could not be executed for executive reasons, because the developments unfolded very quickly. So we did not simply have time to carry out some of these orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's -- in reference to what you just noted, let me show you the next document which is P11 -- P111. If you can look at that very briefly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise what it says, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order for the relief of temporary troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is that related to the previous document that we were looking at that was dated July 14th that was addressed to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I'm told that the document you are holding is P493, so that's a correction from P111. All right. Now, is there anything specific related to your TO units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some things are relevant. I had to single out part of my troops for the execution of that task as well as part of the commanding officers who were to command that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me show you -- let me show you another document, P498, while keeping that document in front of you. If you could look at this. This is an order, is it not, dated 16 July 1995? The relevant paragraph will be paragraph number 7, but first let's just go through the documents.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is an order, is it not, dated 16 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is a day later than the previous document that we've seen that was marked 493. Correct? And if we go to paragraph number 7, can we draw any conclusions from that particular paragraph, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can draw a specific conclusion, as it is specified here, troops from the 1st Infantry Battalion designated to replace personnel at Trnovo will become part of the 1st Infantry Battalion, that means they will not be sent to any other axis or any other mission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So did they go to Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went, together with me, to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we've heard testimony in this courtroom that sometime on the 13th or 14th, the chief of staff, which would have been Major Pajic, Novica Pajic, had gone. And here, both of these documents reflect that they are directed to the chief of staff. Can you help us out here? What's going on? If the chief of staff isn't there, why are these documents being directed to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite clear on that, why he is specifically named in this order, because the order applied to my unit. And in the left bottom corner, as would be usual, it is not indicated to whom the order was addressed. It says the order was addressed to the chief of staff, only for the purpose of archiving the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, speaking of archiving, I just want to go back because I want to pick up a point that we left off yesterday at the end of the day, and that would be with respect to the order of July 14, 1995, regarding the searching of the terrain. And that would be 48 -- P483. When you see the document, you will know which document I am referring to. As you may recall, this was the document that I had you focus your attention on paragraph 1 and thereafter mark on the map that was D186, the coordinates of which you were ordered to search. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in looking at this particular order, again we see that it's addressed to the chief of staff on 14 July 1995, the date when in fact he is supposed to have been out of the Bratunac Brigade area. Can you tell us a little bit about that. Why is it addressed to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand why it was addressed to him, because the person wasn't there. He could have no direct insight or provide his personal contribution to that activity. The only possible explanation for including this addressee is archiving, as I said. But in this order, which is rather particular, both in the sense of its meaning and in the sense that it doesn't comply with the format prescribed by administrative and office rules in the former JNA which we followed, it is not indicated in the left bottom corner to whom it was copied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Why is that important, to whom it would be copied, that is, distributed to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is important to know to whom it was copied for the simple reason that it would confirm that a document was drafted in so many copies and that it was accessible to people to whom it was addressed. Sometimes it would not be actually made available to the persons indicated, but it was important to know that it was done in that many copies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, you've indicated one more shortcoming in this particular document, that's on top of the ones that we spoke about in you pointing out the map yesterday or being requested to search terrain that was already free terrain. Could you please give us an explanation how someone could draft such an order with so many shortcomings.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could have been drafted only by somebody who was insufficiently trained in the military sense. I can give you one more detail. When you designate a battalion's command post, you usually specify whether it is a school building or a junction of roads or an agricultural cooperative, any other building. You usually specify, for instance, the command post for the 2nd Battalion is designated as Potocari village; it is a huge village. And the commander of that battalion could be quite confused. Where is he supposed to set up his command post? As I read this, I cannot but assume that somebody from the operative organ of the brigade wrote this and that he or she did so only pro forma.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Before we talk about that, picking up on the last point where you said under number 2, if forward command post or the command post for the 2nd Battalion is village of Potocari, why don't you make that distinction for paragraph number 1 where it says the command post of the 1st Battalion will be the village of Cizmici? There it designates a village as well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here again, the location is unspecified, but Cizmici village is much smaller than Potocari, so I chose Potocari to better illustrate the deficiencies of paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who in the operations would be -- during that time would be tasked with drafting these sorts of orders or these sorts of documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who the person would have been or might have been?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most often it was done by Lieutenant, Junior Lieutenant Micic, Milorad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a trained officer in the sense as you had been trained, that is, with four years secondary military education, plus four years of academy, formal military academy education?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He had finished only secondary military school and at one point in time he was promoted in an extraordinary procedure to an officer's rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why would he have been promoted under such a procedure, in light of his rather slim military educational background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly what the reason was, the proposals were made by the then-brigade command. But I would like to say that -- I don't want to say that he was a bad officer, he was not diligent and responsible; however, his level of education did not provide him with broad views enabling him to deal with this kind of problems, for instance, with designating command posts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says here in the translation that he was a bad, I believe you meant to say he was not a bad -- is that correct, that he was not a bad officer or he was a --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't want to say that he was a bad officer. I heard he was a good, disciplined, conscientious, and responsible officer, apart from the fact that he lacked sufficient training and knowledge for the duties that he discharged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, while we're still at this I want to cover a couple of points. First of all, do you know a Nikola Gajic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us who this gentleman is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a soldier with my battalion for a certain period of time, and he was a member of my reconnaissance platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any point in time authorise him to leave his position and to go into Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, either to him or to anyone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, he was asked concretely about whether there was any activity, combat activity after July 11, 1995. And just for my colleagues here, that could be found on page 3.353 when Ms. Davis questioned Mr. Gajic, specifically line 9 and onwards for the record, for those who may want to check the accuracy of my paraphrasing. Prior to July 9th -- July 11th, you told us there was some activity. You told us about July 9th when one of your men stepped on a landmine. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if my memory serves me correct, those who were involved in those activities were part of the reconnaissance unit, or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you are not wrong. They were members of the reconnaissance units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, lest there be any misunderstanding, the question is, directing your attention to the specific date of July 11th. Okay. From then onwards, was there any other combat activity that the reconnaissance unit was engaged in to your understanding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period between the 9th and the 11th July, if I understood you correctly, this unit did not take any part in any operations. So on the 9th, the 10th, and on the 11th, they never went the defence sector covered by the battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this unit see any combat activity after the 11th? And I'm talking about the 11th, the 12th, the 13th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took part on the 12th. After they entered the Cizmici village on the 13th and the 14th, this unit was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was that -- was there any combat activity, shooting, killings, confronting the enemy during that period, aside from the movement that you've indicated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no confrontation with the enemy, but let me tell you I -- that on the 12th I entered the sector where the abandoned enemy trenches were in order to provide security there. So that means that we did have to have some combat operations in order to prevent any surprises, because we couldn't be absolutely sure that there wasn't anyone, any enemy, awaiting us in the trenches. So sometimes we did open small arms fire, and this is a normal procedure under such circumstances, as a kind of prevention. And we were duty-bound to do that. However, direct confrontation with the enemy did not take place on the 12th, or the 13th, or the 15th or the 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Lastly, Mr. Gajic, when he was here, had marked a map. So I would like to show you this map. It was entered into as an exhibit as P162. If you could please look at it. Incidentally, before we -- before I have you discuss the map, could you please tell us whether Mr. Gajic had any military training, formal academic military training or schooling, such as you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that he only went through regular military training, just like everybody else, but no other military training other than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're talking about the JNA training, the compulsory training that one would have gone through in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you could look at this map, sir, and when you're ready to discuss it after you orient yourself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am ready.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, according to Mr. Gajic's testimony when he was here back on 23 October 2003 being questioned by Ms. Davis on page 3.367, line 6, he was asked to assign the location to the battalion command and the answer was the letter B. So could you please first look at the letter B and tell us whether Mr. Gajic was right when he noted whether that was the location of the battalion command.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What location has he marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see clearly which feature this is, but it's a place unknown to me, and I'm not aware that the command post had ever been set up there, nor could it have been according to the rules. Because this is the right flank of the battalion, and it's illogical to put it there. Normally the command post is set up in the middle of the defence sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, can you look at those lines and try to figure out what those lines mean, that is the C, the A, the D. Do you know what he is marking there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only guess. It seems that there are some segments and elements here that are unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Such as?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm objecting to this. The witness said he can only guess. It's purely speculative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think you have to change the form of your question. You cannot ask the witness to guess what is in another witness's mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's look at what is marked as this line C. Do you see that? Do you recognise that terrain, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And could you please tell us what is being marked there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only recognise some features. Basically this is unclear to me what it is -- this is all about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Where was the 1st Battalion located? Is it located on any of these lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to point C?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm looking -- I'm asking you to look at the map and tell me where on the map would there -- the battalion would have been positioned at that point in time. And we're going to move -- let's just say from the 6th onwards.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. From the 6th onwards the Lomenac creek, Gajici, Lemesac, and then there's another feature here called Stolice. And then trig point -- I can't see clearly here, but it's called Vresinje. Then it descends towards - just let me see here, just a moment, please - to Jezestica and towards trig point 555, called Ilina Bara.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is there a line on the map currently that designates where the -- as you've described it, where the 1st Battalion would have been located on the 6th? Are one of these lines designated, as you have described it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only partly. Only a small portion of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In other words, there isn't one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in this sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you please tell us where the 1st Battalion or elements of the 1st Battalion moved to on the 12th. I believe there was testimony that they moved on the 12th and then on to the 13th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I will start from the right-hand flank, from the feature 555. And as far as Vresinje, there was no movement. As for the remaining units were moved from Vresinje sector to Cizmici village. And approximately up to the Vjeceljska Rijeka. That was what took place on the 12th. Then on the 13th, we linked up with the 2nd Battalion and we went to the sector around 520 trig point, that is the Pale sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is any of that reflected on any of these lines? And if so, which line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only this part, which in fact remained static, is indicated, that is from trig point 555 to Vresinje; whereas, the remaining hasn't been indicated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And the searching of the terrain that you indicated, I believe you began searching some of the terrain on the 16th. Because the 15th, it was raining, and you indicated that you got the order late on the 15th. So can you show us which line, if any, would reflect the searching of the terrain that was carried out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no line reflecting the direction of our movement at that time, except for this part here where we eventually concentrated in the areas around the villages of Jaglici and Lupoglav on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we look at what is designated as D, can you identify that location for us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the village of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How close were you to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as the crow flies it would be at least 5 kilometres; whereas, on the ground it's a much bigger distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And again, where was your command post? If you could point that out. Can you locate your command post? You indicated that B was not it. Could you perhaps mark it with a -- with an E, where your command post would be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe this was marked by another witness. I'm not sure if it would be appropriate for him to mark the same map at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you. You have to furnish the witness with another copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have, Your Honour. I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: With different numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. It's a little early in the morning, Your Honour, but I did catch myself on that. I have another one. Here you go. This can be marked for identification as D188/1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you mark it? Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is rather imprecise. The tolerance would be plus/minus 100 metres to the right or the left, but this is approximately the location. And on top of that, the copy is rather bad, but definitely it wasn't the position B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you told us it's approximately 5 kilometres away. Could you please tell us what the terrain looked like.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Behind my lines, the terrain was before that, laden with mines, and we avoided the whole area, particularly on the right flank. I can't say that it was totally inaccessible, but it was a difficult terrain to negotiate. It's a hilly land and crises-crossed with ravines and creeks which can be seen from the map as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the E that you've designated, that's the command post at what point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the command post all the way up to the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the 12th of July, where was the new command post placed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the village of Cizmici sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would be where the C is located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from Cizmici to Kravica, what's the distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a -- very far away, approximately perhaps 10 or 15 kilometres. I don't see the scale here that I can -- that can help me. And this is the distance as the crow flies; on the ground, it's much farther. Because when one goes on the ground, you have to go uphill and downhill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, looking at D, which is Kravica, could you please tell us where would Glogova be. Would it be heading west or heading east?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the east.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it possible for you to approximate where it would be or to find where it is on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Glogova is a big village or, rather, the whole area is called Glogova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a kind of geographical term.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you ever in Glogova during this period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's -- I mean the witness can't possibly answer that question; it's totally speculative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the question may be speculative, but they were slanderous, nonetheless, and irresponsible comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's very difficult to say at this stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to show you the map -- go back to the map of D186. And we have this original map. We can take those other ones away. Okay. If I could focus your attention again to where your lines were, and this time I would like to make reference to a report. It's called the "Srebrenica Military Narrative" by Mr. Butler. If I could make some reference. I have the relevant pages for the ELMO. First -- well, perhaps we can -- we'll have to work out the logistics here. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, you have to bear in mind that this witness is a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is it possible for this document not to show --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible. Yes, absolutely. Absolutely -- well, I was doing it for the benefit of everyone here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did the 1st -- do you know whether the 1st Infantry Battalion command controlled or manned any part of the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it goes on to state that the "1st Battalion had a historical responsibility for this particular area from just west of Bratunac toward Kravica. Since mid-1993 when the line stabilised and after the declaration of the Srebrenica safe area, this unit was responsible for this geographical area. This remained true through at least 16th July 1995." And then it goes on: "However, while responsible for part of the area, Kravica and Sandici fell specifically in the zone of the 4th Infantry Battalion." Now, let me focus your attention on this. Going back to what he says that: "There was a historical responsibility for this particular area from just west of Bratunac toward Kravica," did this battalion have this "historical responsibility," as Mr. Butler would have us believe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it sounds as an exaggeration, this poetical term "historical responsibility." I simply don't understand it. Some areas are mentioned here. I said a couple of words about that yesterday, but I can say again; a battalion does not have a zone of responsibility. Not even the brigade has one. A battalion has an area of defence. And whether it can be held responsible for a certain part of the area of defence depends on whether we have enough power. We were not even able, in our specific case, to control even that road. I, for instance, experienced an ambush on that road where some of my men were killed. The road was impossible to control, so that claim absolutely doesn't stand up to scrutiny.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we look at the map, just so we understand this, this historical responsibility that Butler claims the 1st Battalion had, he says: "Just west from Bratunac toward Kravica." Can you find where Bratunac is and we can go westward from Bratunac towards Kravica, so at least we can see where Butler has placed your historical responsibility to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bratunac, the Bratunac town is here. My battalion was on these positions. The 4th Battalion was there. And Kravica is right there. So it was even behind the lines of the 4th Battalion, to the right of the 4th Battalion. And even if you look far into the depth, Kravica could not count as a part of our area of defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But just again, because we need to have a clear record, first of all, point Bratunac out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And we will be able to locate Bratunac on the map. And just refresh our memories. Where were your lines as of the 12th of July, before you moved them, that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the 6th, they were in Lomenac Brook, exclusive; Pajici; Lemesac; there is another feature here, Stolice; trig point 532, Vresinje; and over here is Jezestica; and trig point 555, Ilina Bara, exclusive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Incidentally, when you were -- you were questioned, were you not, by the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall Mr. Butler being there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever asked any questions with respect to -- with respect to where the lines were at the time when he asked you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's one of these maps that I marked, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Because we're going to get to another map at some point. Now, I want to look at another section of Mr. Butler's report and ask you some questions. And this is with respect to -- and I'm referring to page 57 and 58. In particular, I want to read you a portion and see if you could help us out here. I'm reading from page 58, top of the page. This is part of paragraph 6.40. And it's in the -- again, the narrative. And I don't have the number available at this time, for the record, but we'll get it. It says: "On the basis of this order" -- this is the order of the 13th that we looked at earlier, "the command of the Bratunac Brigade issued order 453-2 dated 13th of July." That was the order we looked at earlier this morning. "This order signed by the brigade commander, Colonel Vidoje Blagojevic, directed all four battalions to conduct sweep operations in various areas, specific to the 1st and 4th Battalion operating to the south of the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje road, the following instructions were given." Now, based on the order that we looked earlier, were you asked to conduct any sweeping operations south of the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand, first of all, this term "clearing" or "sweeping." What is it supposed to imply? If a ground search, terrain search, is meant, our task was to search the terrain to the south of the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then he goes on to say that -- he specifically quotes from the order that we read which says: "The 1st Infantry Battalion will search the terrain of the former enclave of Srebrenica on the right side." And it talks about the junction of "Bratunac/Konjevic Polje/Jezestica road K316." So are we talking south of the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje road? If you look at those trig points from the order that we've discussed earlier and you look at the map, is that south of the Konjevic Polje road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is south.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I want to go to the -- another exhibit that has come in. And this would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, are these exhibits related to the Butler report?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, this is a separate exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Oh, I apologise. I didn't notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we'll have a break and we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, are you finishing your direct examination in this session?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Soon, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before we -- while we still have the map there, could you tell us -- you told us where your lines were. Could you show us where your second echelon units were located, since you were in a decisive defence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even have the second echelon. I did not have a company in this second defence line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would be necessary, would it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for clarifying that. Now, if we could go through what has been marked as P91. And if I could just focus your attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We won't be needing that map any longer -- at least we won't be needing it right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could focus your attention to July 3rd, and perhaps we can keep this off the ELMO. But just look at July 3rd. Do you see the first paragraph in these notes dated 3 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And is that an accurate description of the events as they were unfolding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything that you wish to comment on with respect to this meeting that took place on 3 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe this point on which I kept insisting all the time so that we get assistance to reinforce the movements of military patrols around town so that our defence line be filled to capacity at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Are you referring to -- well, for lack of a better term deserters, or soldiers that would leave their lines without authorisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We call it absent without official leave. There were many reasons why people abandoned their positions. 80 per cent, for instance, of my battalion were men whose houses had burnt during the attacks by the 28th Division, because as you well know all the villages around Bratunac had been burned down by the forces commanded by Naser Oric. Those people were very hard up. And it happened sometimes that they had to go home to do some work in their fields so that they could earn a living. However, that was a problem for me because I had to ensure combat readiness. And I always lacked personnel to be engaged for this task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidentally, did you have any soldiers who came from villages that were in the territories controlled by the Muslim forces that became somewhat liberated after the 11th or 12th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had some soldiers from those villages, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we could go on to July 5, 1995, it says -- the point that I wish to bring out to your attention and perhaps you can comment on it. It says: "The chief of staff will go to the 1st Battalion to increase accuracy and direction of artillery fire." This is 5 July 1995. Do you know whether the chief of staff did in fact go or come to the 1st Infantry Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please explain to us what exactly was the purpose, what does this entail "increase accuracy and direction of artillery fire"? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a usual organisational task that is performed in order to arrange the firing system. Namely, particular weapons are assigned the direction of fire or even an area of fire, depending on the calibre. Decisions are made as to where to lay minefields as to have better engineering on the positions, achieve coordination, things like that. This is some kind of preventive work so that at a given moment the complete system of defence could work properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If we could go on to July 16th, and incidentally let me correct myself. This is D165 as opposed to P91, as I had made reference to earlier, this document. Here it indicates that the: "1st Battalion at full strength to be given task in the area of combat activity in Zepa." Did that occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I believe we talked about the previous orders that one was for you to send men to Trnovo, and then it was cancelled the next day. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we could go to October 16, 1995, I want you to look at -- if we could locate that page, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look at the very last sentence in this page. All right. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see. Some things are illegible, but I can assume what it's about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me read it for you. Under "Nikolic," that would be Momir Nikolic. I assume you knew the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And it says: "We are currently engaged in tasks issued by the Army of Republika Srpska General Staff," and in parentheses it says, "sanitation," though I believe in Srpski, it says asanacija. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we were to look above as to who attended the meeting, it would appear that you were present at this meeting, were you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want you to roll back the film to 16 October 1995, if that is possible, and please tell us what, if anything, you recall with respect to this that was being mentioned by Mr. Nikolic at that period.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Was there a discussion, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were any questions posed as to why the General Staff -- why Nikolic was engaged on activity or tasked by the General Staff, since he was a member of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No questions were asked of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, I want to go to another set of documents. First, we'll go to a map, a map that has been prominently displayed, much discussed. And I'm referring to P369. I believe I have the only copy. If we could look at this map. First, perhaps we could -- if you could move it from -- and then perhaps we could show the first part -- there you go. Thank you, sir. Now, have you seen this map before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember if maybe the Prosecution showed me the map before, but the map basically says nothing to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We're going to go step by step. All right. First of all, we see some official lettering on this and it reflects that this is the -- this is a map of the zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade. And we see the name of a Colonel Zivanovic who was the then-commander of the Drina Corps. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- so at least we have a title of this map, do we not? On this map we have a title?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It shows that Colonel Zivanovic -- it has Colonel Zivanovic's name. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, first of all during those days did you ever see this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Secondly, is this map an official map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First, tell us why it is your opinion that this is not an official map, even though it says "zone of responsibility, Colonel Zivanovic." We have those names; we have the title.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the many shortcomings in the map. First of all, if it had been approved, it should have been signed by Colonel Zivanovic and certified by a stamp. Secondly --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Polako, polako. Where would that be? Where would the signature be and where would the stamp be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The signature would be here next to the name, so would the stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Next. What's the next problem with this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next flaw in the upper right-hand corner, there should be, in addition to what there is already, the degree of confidentiality, it should have said when the map was -- began and when it was completed. And also it should specify the period of how long this map should be kept on file. That is also missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So it would have a beginning and an end date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about the title? I mean, it's large --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The title is incorrect because a brigade, as a joint tactical unit, is not assigned any area of responsibility. If it is on the defence, it has a defence zone or vice versa, an offensive zone. According to our rules that we adhered to and that we still adhere to, only these two categories exist for a brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's look at this geographical area that is purported to be the zone of responsibility. And maybe you can help us out here. First of all, where is the Drina River so we can orient ourselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that would be the boundary, would it not, between Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia, the Drina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so now if you're at the Drina, we're going westwards into Bosnia. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at the western, the western-most line on the zone. You go all the way out west and you see the last -- the line, where is that and what is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a zone that encompasses even the area of Srebrenica, which is also illogical, which area until 1995 was not under our control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Anything else that you see wrong with this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this map should have been signed by an appropriate officer or organ that drafted the map, including the title of the person in charge and also the signature of the officer. This is also missing on the map. In addition to that, these border lines that somebody has drawn - and I don't know the product of whose imagination that is - I'm not quite sure what they represent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where would the signature, the name and the signature of the author, the creator, the genius behind this map, where would that be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name of this genius should be in the bottom right-hand corner, the signature, and plus a legend should be included here, indicating or explaining what these markings mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, while we have the map here let me ask you: Are there any specific rules that give guidance as to what is and what is not an official map for military purposes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are rules.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, perhaps we can look at those rules to see whether this map comports with the rules. Let me show you what is marked as D184. And I would like you to look at the instructions on working maps in the armed forces. Do you have them, sir, in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it says here that -- it has a date of 1979. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we go all the way up it says: "Federal Secretariat for National Defence." And it's even a military secret.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm just wondering if Mr. Karnavas can tell us where he got this document. There's no ERN number on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, this document we received from one of the officers. We provided this document to the Office of the Prosecution months ago; we translated it for them, so they have it. I'm trying to lay the proper foundation at this point in time. But these are official rules which were available to the Prosecution prior to us coming here today to make reference to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, could you be more specific. You said: "We received from one of the officers." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, it was one of the witnesses who has already I believe come in through 92 bis. And if my memory serves me correct, Your Honour, it was Officer Goran Lazarevic. He's on the list of 92 bis. It's a book, just like all the other books that we've seen. Usually it's red with a little star; that's common for that period. We had the original book itself. We copied it, and then we had it translated. So Mr. Butler, had he been -- you know, had he been careful enough, he would have asked for that particular book as well because all the other books he's copied we seem to have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, is it a procedural issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah, it just has to do with the history and just to respond to that. We do not have -- and looking at our records haven't received any of this stuff. We may be able to work that out between us ourselves at the break. And we have had a very difficult time getting these books over the years, extremely difficult. They are sensitive books, so the comments about Mr. Butler are really not appropriate. But we just want to know -- I don't doubt Mr. Karnavas has got these books from some source and that they are likely legitimate. We would just like to have some background on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think you furnish those books or at least a copy of this book to the other party a month before?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. When we received it -- we received the physical book itself from the gentleman, and he's still serving so he makes reference to them. We received it. We copied it. We provided the original version. And then we had the -- we had it even translated officially. And then we provided the translation to the Office of the Prosecution. Now, had the Prosecutor asked me to provide or to show them the original, I would have been able to borrow it. I don't have it physically. I haven't purchased it; I don't know if I can. But I have seen it. The gentleman, Goran Lazarevic, you will note in his 92 bis statement, there's also a map attached to it. He makes reference to this -- to these instructions as well. It won't be a problem if they want to check the copies that we've provided. I can make arrangements to have -- to show him the -- an original book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And those documents or instructions are the official documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, it's official -- it's bounded just like all the other instructions we have on the brigade. I'm also going to be referring to a battalion manual. This also has been translated and it also has been provided to the -- this may have an ERN number, I think. But yes, it's an official document. If you look at the -- if you just compare the manuals, you'll see they all look the same. They all have the little star and it all has the same language. And this is part of the JNA material that the VRS used at that period of time. And that's what I was going to go into.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We never received one of those. It's probably just an inadvertent discovery situation, which as we know both sides have. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is -- it's not such an easy subject when you're talking about these things. If I recollect one of the military experts was highly critical of Mr. Butler regarding his discussion of whether or not the rules and regulations of the former JNA were used or used as guidelines for this case. And so I'm sure this witness can help us on that subject. But it's a little difficult when we do not have the books or the translations of the books. But again, I have no reason to believe this has been any -- is anything more than an oversight and I don't have any problem with us going forward as long as we can get together when this is over and try to get this material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. Mr. Karnavas, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'll apologise to the Prosecution if they haven't received it. I was told that they have received them. Obviously there is a glitch, but that won't be a problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could just draw your attention to that document, sir. First of all, I want to lay a foundation. Have you seen these instructions on working maps in the armed forces before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And where have you seen them, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my schooling and later in my career I used it while I discharged the duties of an operational training organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know, sir, whether these instructions - and we have -- they are dated 1979 - were they, in fact, being used by the VRS back in 1995, or 1992 I should say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who knew about this, applied it. And those who didn't, just like those who drew these maps, didn't use it because obviously they didn't know of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you what I'm trying to get more concretely. Did the JNA adopt other instructions, other than the ones that you have in front of you, or were these instructions the official instructions on working maps for the JNA -- for the VRS? I apologise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you have the whole set. And just so that the Prosecution knows, we asked only that the pertinent parts be copied -- I mean be translated, although we have the full contents of this document, the table of contents. If you could look at the rules and point to us which rules are pertinent when we want to determine whether this map, the one that we looked at, has any validity or not.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 22, item 25 of the instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That would be on page 14 of the English. And we're looking at numbered paragraph 25. Okay. Please comment then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It specifies here exactly who and what kind of maps are made and by whom. And it enumerates the working map of the commander, of the staff, of combat army organs, of service organs, of political activity organs. That's the one that we didn't have, in fact, because it was outdated. Then the map of the intelligence organ, of the security organ, for coordinated action, and what it says here in the translation, a clear map with a question mark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go step by step. This paragraph 25, this deals with what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 25 deals only with listing the types of maps prepared by the then-JNA and afterwards by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then are there any paragraphs within these instructions that specifically deal with each one of these items, that is, what is a working map of the commander, a working map of the staff, and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On page 23, para 28 explains what the working map of the commander is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we don't need to go through all these paragraphs that deal with what each map should contain. But in looking at the title of this map, "zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade," do you know under which of these listed titles this map would fit in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say who could draw a zone of responsibility, which, as I emphasised, did not exist as a term. So I have no idea who could possibly have made this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what I'm asking you is: From A to J, which one of these would this map fit in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under none of these items.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And prior to coming here today, have you looked over the various paragraphs that give the detailed descriptions of what each of these maps require, that is, the map of the commander, map of staff, map of combat arms organs? Have you looked at that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I used to use this instruction in my career, so I am familiar with what each type of map under a specific title should contain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, what other articles do you think are relevant or would be relevant in determining the validity of this particular map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 44, paragraph 74.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What does that tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says what the finalised working map should contain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 28, sir. All right. If you give us one moment here to locate it. Maybe we can move it up the ELMO a little bit -- no, because we're looking at 74. Further up. There you go. So -- and this is under -- this is again D184 for identification. And we're looking at paragraph 74. And above it, it says: "Establishing the working map." All right. Now, could you please tell us why is 74 pertinent.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is pertinent because it shows what in general the map, that any working map must contain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And in fact, if we go on to 75, 76, and 77, we even see more detailed information and even some examples, do we not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is there any other paragraph that is relevant, that might be useful for us in determining whether the map has any value?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 77 confirms what I said earlier, that each map must be signed by stating the rank, the position, and the full name of the signatory. What I would also like to add that if we were to analyse each of the earlier drawn maps that I mentioned under para 25, and if we make a comparison with this map, none of these maps can be considered proper because the one that we have on the ELMO does not correspond to the contents prescribed. It has no context as such. It has no basic information. It does not say where the command post is, where the enemy forces are. It is completely unclear. I really can't understand what can anyone possibly deduce from this map, except for some lines that were drawn on the map. But other than that, I just can't understand what it represents itself. It has no content.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you talked about that the map would also have a legend.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would be in that legend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A legend would contain certain explanations, depending on whether it's for the defensive or offensive purposes. Sometimes it contains the textual and table parts. In the legend it says how the task at hand is marked, how the immediate task is designated, the direction of the battalion movements. Some signs or marks for better understanding or maybe some less ordinary signs that will help you read the map more accurately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I believe that's all I have with this particular map and this instruction or these instructions. And just a couple of houseclearing matters, because I want to be as precise as we can. Let me show you what has been marked as D183. And this is -- just, please, look at it first. Do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us what it is first.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a battalion manual specifying what kind of battalions it refers to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my schooling, that was one of the basic documents that we studied. And after I finished my education, I frequently had this manual in my hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and this would be the official manual, would it not, that was being used at the time that you were in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in your testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Sorry for interrupting, but just wondering where Mr. Karnavas got this manual from as well, just like to know whether it's another source or the same source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps we can go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session. I think that private session is enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for my peace of mind, would this be the kind of manual that an officer would have with him in the field?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in peacetime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And again, is this the kind of manual that would be used at the academy? So, for instance, if I went to Belgrade to the academy and I wanted to get a hold of this manual, would I be able to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have a great aptitude for that academy; maybe one day you'll graduate. But this is a basic book of rules which are followed in following certain courses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just incidentally, when you were in Banja Luka, were you ever asked to produce any working manuals, you know, that you would use on a day-to-day basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not required.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in your testimony - I just want to draw you back to the point where we veered off - you've repeatedly indicated that there's no such thing as a zone of responsibility. You talked about it for -- at the brigade level and you also were very specific about it at the battalion level. Could you point us out to any particular paragraphs in this manual that may give any weight, support, to what you've told us here under oath.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I want to go step by step. Just give us the number and give us a little time to find it. Just tell us the number of the paragraph; that's a little easier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 164, para 320.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That would be page 99, sir. I take it the Prosecution can follow it with their copy of this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what is -- what area is it that you wish to direct our attention to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish to draw everyone's attention to the fact that it's emphasised here that a battalion receives an area of defence, as opposed to a zone of responsibility. It is emphasised that in depth it covers one defence position of the high unit. Also in para 321, which is the next paragraph, it is underlined that: "The width of the defence area of the battalion on manoeuvrable ground and on the centre of the defence may be 3 to 5 kilometres, whereas the depth may be 2 to 3 kilometres."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when we're speaking about a defence area, we're talking about a particular line that has a length and a depth. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And so I take it if we were to go back to the earlier map, the earlier map that you had worked on yesterday, we would be able to - and we're not going to go through it just yet - but if you were to go through this, you would be able to show us the depth of your line. You were able to draw the length. And then based on this, you would be able to show us the depth of your line pursuant to the rules. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So go on. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this rule, there is a very graphic diagram of deployment of a battalion in an area of defence which shows all the things that a battalion is required to have in order to mount a successful defence. In those days, I have to say, I would have been very happy if I had had all these things. And I would feel safer, because I would have a well-organised firing system. However, I didn't have all these things for various reasons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you here. Let me put this diagram, which isn't the original, just so we know. And I'm going to need you to slow down a little bit because we want to go step by step. This is the diagram that you're referring to. I apologise for not having this translated. Okay. First of all, what does this diagram -- in which -- under which paragraph is this diagram found in the book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In paragraph 320. It is indicated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. So this is -- I know, but in the translation we weren't able to do it. So this diagram is part of paragraph 320?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in looking at this diagram, could you just please explain it to us, what does it -- because we're not military folks around here, so maybe you can help us out. What are we looking at? And go step by step.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the top to the bottom of this diagram, it's emphasised that what is described here is the combat disposition. And on the right hand it says "area of defence." On top, you see this acronym BOS which means combat support. It shows here that it could be up to an equivalent of one platoon. In this area it's the 3rd Platoon of the 3rd Infantry Company. It should be ahead of the line. The next item is this semicircle. These two semicircles indicate companies on the first defence line. Each of them has a width, 1 to 1.5 kilometres, which for the total of the battalion constitutes 3 to 5 kilometres. Typically these companies are also deployed. They have their own platoons on the second line, second echelon platoons. That is very necessary because it gives manoeuvring space to the commander of the company and commander of the platoon. This is a marking for the 4th Anti-Armour Group, anti-tank group. Every modern army should have one. This marking here, this sign, indicates a mortar group. This sign indicates the post of the company commander, where he is located. This sign here designates the battalion anti-armour group, the size of an anti-armour company. The next --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you here for a second. I need you to slow down because it has to be translated. So I take it -- and you were demonstrating on this document which will become part of -- which will be given an exhibit number and have it translated, but you were just referring to the first half of the page. And you were pointing at the left semicircle and the contents that were in that semicircle in what will be marked for identification purposes as D189. I take it the right semicircle would have pretty much the same as the left one. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's go to the bottom half, the second -- the semicircle that's at the bottom half that's below the first two semicircles. Okay. Slowly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-105 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. This semicircle here represents a company in the second line, second-echelon company. As you can see, it is deployed in this way, two platoons forward, one platoon behind. Within the framework of the platoon, two sections are up front, one section is behind. The same organic structure, I already said they have an anti-armour group. At the same level of that second-echelon company would be the command post. This sign here, this triangle marked by 1 designates the command post. In the immediate vicinity of the command post, as a rule, you should have this small sign indicating the firing position of a light artillery rocket platoon of air defence. Right behind that is the firing position of the battalion firing group. And behind all of them is the logistical platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
